title: The intention
intro: A fast is more than going without food. This lesson covers the intention behind it: the part that is reported as agreed, and where the primers of the schools place it differently.

claims.text: A fast is kept with an intention: Ibn Rushd gives this as the position of the great majority and names one early jurist, Zufar, who held otherwise for Ramadan. Ibn al-Mundhir reports agreement that someone who intends the fast on each night of Ramadan, and then fasts, has a complete fast.

positions.text: Fasting is holding back from eating, drinking and intercourse by day, together with the intention.
positions.quote: والصوم هو الإمساك عن الأكل والشرب والجماع نهارا مع النية

positions.text: The obligatory parts of the fast are four: the intention, and holding back from eating and drinking, from intercourse, and from deliberate vomiting.
positions.quote: وفرائض الصوم أربعة أشياء النية والإمساك عن الأكل والشرب والجماع وتعمد القيء

cards.front: Besides holding back from food, drink and intercourse, what does a fast need?
Which way of making the intention for Ramadan does Ibn al-Mundhir report as agreed to be enough?
cards.back: Intending the fast on each night of the month.

claims.text: Intending each night is enough by agreement. The primers differ on whether a later intention counts for a Ramadan fast, and on whether one intention can cover the month. The Shafi’i and Hanbali primers used here do not give a time.

positions.text: One kind of obligatory fast is tied to a set time, such as the fast of Ramadan and a vow for a named day: it is valid with an intention made at night. If he has not intended by morning, an intention made between then and midday is enough.
positions.quote: منه ما يتعلق بزمان بعينه كصوم رمضان والنذر المعين فيجوز صومه بنية من الليل فإن لم ينو حتى أصبح أجزأته النية ما بينه وبين الزوال

positions.text: He makes the intention at night at the start of the month, and does not have to make it at night for the rest of it.
positions.quote: ويبيت الصيام في أوله وليس عليه البيات في بقيته

cards.front: Where do the Hanafi and Maliki primers differ on the intention for Ramadan?
cards.back: Hanafi: an intention made before midday is still enough. Maliki: it is made at night, once at the start of the month, and need not be repeated each night.

cards.front: Hanafi primer: no intention was made by morning in Ramadan. Until when can it still be made?
Maliki primer: when is the intention for Ramadan made, and how often?
cards.back: At night, at the start of the month; it need not be made again each night.

check.q: Which way of making the intention is reported as agreed to be enough?
options: Intending the fast each night of Ramadan
Intending at sunset when the fast ends

check.q: In the Hanafi primer, an intention for a Ramadan fast can still be made:
In the Maliki primer, the intention at night is made:
options: at the start of the month, without having to repeat it nightly
only on the last ten nights
